entities.summary: Lucius Funisulanus Vettonianus was a Roman general and senator who played a significant role in the Flavian dynasty's reign from 69 to 96 CE. Born in unknown circumstances, he rose through the ranks of the Roman army and became suffect consul in 78 CE, serving alongside Quintus Corellius Rufus. His military campaigns expanded the Roman Empire's borders, and he was instrumental in suppressing the Bar Kokhba revolt. Despite his significant achievements, his life and legacy remain somewhat overshadowed by those of his contemporaries. Vettonianus's contributions to Roman politics and military strategy have left a lasting impact on the history of the empire, cementing his place as a notable figure in the annals of Roman history.
